R0029.title: Denial of Service Risk
R0029.definition: Slowing down or stopping business responses by sending large numbers of requests to a server or exploiting server vulnerabilities.
R0029.description: Also known as DoS. A denial of service attack is when an attacker causes a target machine to stop providing services. Consuming network bandwidth is only a small part of denial of service attacks — any action that causes trouble for the target, suspends services, or crashes the host qualifies as a denial of service attack.
R0029.influence: Causes business denial of service and affects user access.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-015 Denial of Service

observables: Request volume to the same endpoint or multiple endpoints spikes within a short window, far exceeding the normal baseline
Request source IPs are either highly dispersed or concentrated in data centers and proxy exits, with anomalous QPS
Server CPU, memory, bandwidth, or connection counts are rapidly saturated, with rising response latency and timeout rates

R0029-001.title: SMS Resource Exhaustion
R0029-001.definition: Bulk requesting SMS verification codes and controlling the recipients to exhaust the application's SMS verification code resources while disrupting legitimate users.
R0029-001.description: Sending SMS verification code requests to the same phone number to cause disruption or denial of service, or sending SMS verification codes to large numbers of phone numbers to exhaust service resources. In cases where the content can be controlled, this can also trigger fraud.
R0029-001.influence: Exhausts platform SMS verification code resources, creates a denial of service attack against the server, and causes disruption and denial of service to specific phone number recipients.

references.title: What to Do When SMS Verification Code Interface Is Under Malicious Attack?

observables: The SMS verification code sending endpoint is hit at high frequency, with a single phone number receiving large volumes of verification codes in a short window
The same batch of phone number ranges is bulk-requested, with sending volume severely mismatched against normal user registration volume
SMS gateway cost spikes in a short window, delivery rates drop, and messages are intercepted following carrier complaints

R0029-002.title: Resource Exhaustion Attack
R0029-002.definition: Also known as malicious resource consumption attacks, the goal is to exhaust the target system's resources — such as computing power, storage space, network bandwidth, or other system resources — to paralyze, slow down, or prevent the system from providing normal services.
R0029-002.description: Possible scenarios include: network bandwidth attacks flooding the target network; compute resource exhaustion through computationally intensive requests; storage resource exhaustion by uploading large volumes of invalid or large files; TCP connection attacks (SYN flood); and database resource attacks through mass database queries.
R0029-002.influence: Causes service unavailability, performance degradation, reliability impact, and financial losses due to malicious resource consumption.

references.title: Governance Path for Advertising-Promotion Cyber Black-Grey Crime

observables: Server CPU, memory, disk, or bandwidth utilization stays saturated for extended periods, triggering resource alerts
Large volumes of invalid or large files are uploaded, with disk space filling up rapidly
Database connection counts or slow queries surge, and TCP half-open connections rise anomalously
Network-layer traffic shows SYN/UDP/ICMP flood characteristics

R0029-003.title: CC Attack
R0029-003.definition: Performing a denial of service attack on a system by constructing large numbers of normal business requests.
R0029-003.description: By analyzing each type of business request and targeting requests that are computationally expensive for the server, sending large numbers of forged requests to saturate all server computing resources.
R0029-003.influence: Causes business denial of service and affects user access.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT-015 Denial of Service

observables: Request volume to compute-intensive endpoints (search, sort, complex queries) spikes anomalously
Requests appear to be normal business traffic but access specific endpoints at high frequency to consume compute resources
Source IPs are dispersed but request patterns are highly consistent, bypassing basic rate-limiting rules

R0029-004.title: Distributed Denial of Service
R0029-004.definition: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) is a network attack that uses multiple attackers (or multiple attack sources) to simultaneously attack a target system, rendering it unable to provide normal services.
R0029-004.description: DDoS attacks typically aim to push the target system's network bandwidth, computing resources, or other critical resources to their limits, causing service unavailability. Attack types include: network layer attacks (UDP flood, ICMP flood, SYN/ACK attacks); transport layer attacks (SYN flood); application layer attacks (HTTP request flood, Slowloris); and reflection/amplification attacks.
R0029-004.influence: Causes service unavailability, performance degradation, reliability impact, and financial losses due to resource consumption.

references.title: Understanding and Responding to Distributed Denial-of-Service Attacks - CISA

observables: Ingress bandwidth is saturated in a short window, with traffic sources highly distributed across multiple regions
Traffic shows characteristics of UDP/ICMP/SYN floods or reflection-amplification attacks
Application-layer HTTP request floods originate from large numbers of different IPs, with low per-IP rates but a massive aggregate volume
Service availability drops sharply, and legitimate user connections are rejected in large numbers
